definition: English profanity present in current text, including common censored/obfuscated forms and unlisted profane words. Quoting/reporting counts as surface presence, not author endorsement. Substrings inside ordinary words or identifiers do not count.
provenance: Codex-authored synthetic examples created on 2026-10-30 for this repository; no private dataset or customer text. Developed alongside the analyzer, not a held-out evaluation.

cases.rationale: A literal expletive appears in the current text.
Capitalization does not remove a literal profane word.
A profane word describes the demo.
A literal profane insult is present; this label does not assess harassment.
A common inflected profanity is present.
Punctuation separates the expletive from surrounding text.

cases.text: Those assholes took the last tickets.
cases.rationale: A plural profane word is present.
A literal profane adjective is present.
Quoting preserves surface profanity without establishing the author's intent.
Reporting abuse still places the profane token in the current text.
Educational mention counts as surface presence, not author-directed abuse.
Quoted language is counted literally under this dataset definition.
An expletive outside the deliberately narrow shipped vocabulary tests lexical coverage.
A profane insult outside the shipped vocabulary is still a positive diagnostic label.
An unlisted inflection tests whether vocabulary coverage is complete.
An unlisted profane compound tests the limits of whole-token matching.
A censored profanity tests a capability the literal detector does not implement.
Digit substitution preserves the intended profanity in this diagnostic label.
Punctuation-separated spelling tests evasion handling.

cases.text: f u c k that noise.
cases.rationale: Spaced spelling tests a deliberately unsupported form.
A zero-width space splits an otherwise profane word.
Fullwidth characters test a Unicode normalization capability that is not implemented.
A combining mark tests unsupported decorated spelling.
A second masked spelling tests censored profanity without changing labels to fit output.

cases.text: The classroom is ready for the exhibition.
cases.rationale: An ordinary sentence has no profanity.

cases.text: I bought shiitake mushrooms for dinner.
cases.rationale: A food name is not a profane token.

cases.text: The shuttle to Scunthorpe leaves at noon.
cases.rationale: A place name must not be classified from an internal substring.

cases.text: Their analysis is critical of the product.
cases.rationale: Product criticism alone is not profanity.
Disagreement is not a profane expression.

cases.text: The dam controls the river level.
cases.rationale: A literal dam is not the expletive damn.

cases.text: Please attach the assignment before Friday.
cases.rationale: An ordinary word containing an insult-like substring remains benign.

cases.text: The ticket is already closed, thanks.
cases.rationale: A routine status update has no profanity.

cases.text: Look up SHIT123 in the inventory.
cases.rationale: This example labels an inventory identifier rather than an independent profane word.
Underscores keep this identifier together under the stated label definition.
Brackets separate a literal profane token.
Emoji and punctuation surround a literal token; evidence must preserve UTF-16 offsets.
